clinician.final_diagnosis: Transient acetylcholine receptor-related myasthenia gravis occurring shortly after MIS-C
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 7-year-old girl presented with 4 days of fever, sore throat, cough, diarrhoea, headaches, and clinical findings of shock, high fever, bilateral non-suppurative conjunctivitis, erythematous desquamating rash, and swelling of hands and feet. Echocardiography showed reduced left ventricular function with an ejection fraction of 38% and no coronary aneurysms. Laboratory data supported MIS-C diagnosis with multiorgan failure requiring ICU support, positive SARS-CoV-2 antibodies, and raised inflammatory markers (not specifically quantified in the record). After PICU discharge, the patient developed proximal muscle weakness with a positive Gower sign, waddling gait, lumbar lordosis, and preserved deep tendon reflexes. Creatine kinase was elevated at 6617 u/L, and acetylcholine receptor antibodies were positive (titre 0.51 nmol/L, normal <0.39 nmol/L), supporting a diagnosis of myasthenia gravis. Clinical course details confirm a temporal association and onset of transient acetylcholine receptor-related myasthenia gravis following MIS-C.
